children: Indian markets may be pricing in a much more aggressive Reserve Bank of India tightening cycle than warranted by the economy, according to Nomura, which expects just 50 basis points of rate hikes by December against nearly 125 basis points currently priced in over the next year.

Nomura expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points each in October and December to 5.75 percent, but says the moves would amount to a “preemptive recalibration” rather than the start of a full tightening cycle. The brokerage argues that while food and energy prices could push inflation higher over the next six months, there are limited signs of broader inflationary pressures.
Why Nomura thinks markets are overpricing rate hikes

The RBI’s monetary policy is at an “inflection point”, Nomura said, but it believes the current cycle is different from a conventional inflation-led tightening cycle. “Markets are pricing close to 125bp of rate hikes over the next one year, but our analysis suggests this cycle is fundamentally different,” the brokerage said.

Nomura pointed to a moderation in India’s trend inflation and said its “inflation generalization index confirms no signs of broadening”. At the same time, its leading index is signalling “below-trend growth ahead”. This combination, according to Nomura, reduces the need for the central bank to embark on a prolonged rate-hike cycle.

The brokerage expects inflation to rise in the near term because of higher food and energy prices, but said these pressures could eventually weigh on demand and help bring inflation lower. “We expect the cyclical pressures from food and energy prices to push up inflation over the next six months, but as they dampen demand, inflation should return to target,” Nomura said.
Two hikes, not a full tightening cycle

Nomura expects the RBI to raise rates by 25 basis points in both October and December, taking the repo rate to a terminal level of 5.75 percent. The brokerage sees these hikes as an attempt to keep inflation expectations anchored rather than the beginning of an aggressive tightening cycle. “Given limited signs of generalization, a full tightening cycle is unlikely,” Nomura said.

It described the expected rate increases as a “preemptive recalibration to anchor expectations” and added that “the RBI will do less in this cycle, not more”. Nomura expects CPI inflation to average 5.2 percent in FY27 before easing to the RBI’s 4 percent midpoint target in FY28.
Food, energy prices key near-term risk

The brokerage expects food and energy prices to remain the main source of inflation pressure over the coming months. However, it does not see these pressures translating into a broad-based inflation problem. Instead, Nomura expects higher prices to eventually weaken demand, helping inflation return towards target.
This is a key reason behind its view that the RBI would not need to match the nearly 125 basis points of rate hikes currently priced by markets.

On the currency front, Nomura expects the rupee to remain supported by a combination of high energy prices, expectations of further US Federal Reserve hikes and rising US Treasury yields in the near term. Over the medium term, however, the brokerage expects the rupee to underperform the euro.

It cited three factors behind this view: RBI accumulation of US dollars, portfolio flow challenges and pressures from the current account deficit. Nomura also expects the US dollar to weaken over the medium term.

title: Markets pricing 125 bps RBI hikes, but Nomura says bets are too aggressive; sees just 50 bps
